Session id resolution (src/utils/session.ts, deriveSession — one pure function decides id + shared + detected together): RVR_SESSION → the harness's own session var when its env fingerprint matches (#207; Claude Code: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) → per-process random. A shared id (explicit or detected) switches on the disk-backed CLI guardrails in sessionState.ts: write-amp window and miss-path tracking, one state file per session under <dataDir>/sessions/.

GOTCHAS:
- Detect the HARNESS from the env (detectHarness), never from the resolved agent: deriveAgentIdentity returns early when RVR_AGENT_NAME is set, and the fleet sets it everywhere — a fallback built on the agent name never fires on a fleet machine.
- The suite runs inside Claude Code (no test job on PRs). _setup.ts scrubs HARNESS_SESSION_VARS; without it 8 tests fail and a session file leaks into the shared tmp data dir. Spawns inherit the scrub only through { ...process.env } — an env-less spawn does not.
- Adding a harness: add sessionVar to its FINGERPRINTS row; the scrub and detection follow. Codex's variable is unknown.
- The write-amp guard exempts exactly one key, the handoff (isWriteAmpExempt, writeAmp.ts). The check must sit in BOTH recordWrite and recordCliWrite: a shared CLI session calls pruneAndRecord directly (key-agnostic) and never reaches recordWrite — exempting recordWrite alone fixes MCP and misses the Claude Code path.
- The guard counts per (store, key) — writeAmpSlot — and on the CLI only when the handler called markValueStored() after setValue. A new CLI path that stores a value under tool reverie_set and omits the mark is never counted, and nothing enforces it (same trap as context.aliasResolvedCapture).
- Unverified: whether Claude Code subagents share the parent's id (CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION exists) and whether a resumed session keeps it.
- Contended session-file lock waits at most ~31ms, then that call skips its bookkeeping; the command never fails.
